changeHypothesis.summary: Energy-storage demand was strong enough to support battery-cell volumes and lithium economics, but the raw-material price direction was volatile and not a one-way miner thesis. Among battery makers, 亿纬锂能 showed materially faster storage revenue growth than 宁德时代 but much weaker storage margins, leaving a mixed selection edge.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: Storage demand and restocking were independently reported and both major A-share battery makers disclosed material storage businesses.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: Storage growth was already known, while lithium price direction was visibly unstable.
expectations.thesisExpectation: Battery makers with real storage volume growth can benefit even without a one-way lithium-price bet.
expectations.measurableGap: EVE's faster storage growth is measurable, but whether it outweighs its much lower margin and market expectations is unresolved.

expectationBurdenTest.valuationMethod: Segment growth/margin burden plus relative earnings sensitivity; avoid treating lithium price alone as valuation signal.
expectationBurdenTest.marketBaseline: Both companies were established battery leaders and storage demand was public; EVE's faster storage growth alone is not sufficient.
expectationBurdenTest.thesisScenario: EVE sustains >20% storage growth and improves/holds margin despite lithium volatility, producing greater incremental earnings sensitivity than CATL.
expectationBurdenTest.breakevenCondition: EVE must translate its faster storage revenue growth into profit growth sufficient to offset the roughly 14pp storage gross-margin disadvantage versus CATL.
expectationBurdenTest.ordinaryScenarioFailure: Storage volumes rise but low margins persist, making CATL the better economics despite slower segment growth.
